question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` intentionally narrow its existing CLI contract by rejecting equivalent base-10 spellings such as `+500` and `0500`?
rationale: Current code and the shared parser accept these spellings, while public Policy docs define interval behavior but not canonical textual encoding; automation cannot choose the compatibility policy.

options.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
options.body: Keep the existing accepted base-10 spellings and avoid adding a canonical textual identity requirement.

options.title: Require canonical decimal text
options.body: Approve the compatibility break, document the exact syntax, and require real CLI before/after/control proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
recommendation.body: Keep the existing accepted base-10 spellings and avoid adding a canonical textual identity requirement.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and documented the Policy CLI surface whose input contract is being narrowed.
